Collect every original span that independently states, defines, qualifies, authorizes, prohibits, triggers, excepts, or continues the proposition. Follow split sentences and clause chains across adjacent spans when later fragments complete the actor, object, condition, exception, or list. Also scan other sections for independently responsive repetitions. Include a heading or lead-in only when it supplies legally necessary scope; exclude it when it is merely navigational. Exclude adjacent background, examples, and generic confidentiality language that do not resolve the proposition. operations.rationale: Creates a general source-inspection skill because the empty-library observations repeatedly preserved the correct relation while omitting continuation spans, definitions, qualifications, or independently responsive provisions, and also added merely adjacent text. The selected evidence demonstrates split definition chains, a multi-fragment prohibition, repeated purpose restrictions, and definition-plus-exception membership.

guidance.procedure: Normalize the proposition into actor, modality, action, object, trigger, beneficiary, and exception before comparing it with the source. An express prohibition supports a prohibitory proposition but ordinarily opposes a proposition asserting permission. A prohibition subject only to discretionary prior consent is not automatically an affirmative permission; distinguish it from an operative authorization for a defined recipient, purpose, or circumstance. For copying, sharing, retention, return, destruction, solicitation, and reverse engineering, preserve limiting conditions and carve-outs. A return or destruction duty answers an asserted termination trigger only when that trigger is actually operative; a demand or request condition must not be silently rewritten. For post-return possession, inspect backup, archival, dispute, legal-compliance, no-copy, and continuing-confidentiality language together. Cite all spans that form the operative rule and its material exception, but not unrelated confidentiality duties.

operations.rationale: Creates a polarity-and-trigger skill from observed confusion between permissions and qualified prohibitions, and between termination-triggered duties and request-conditioned duties. The witnesses preserve opposed boundaries: retention allowed by a carve-out versus barred by complete delivery, copying expressly allowed when necessary versus prohibited, and defined sharing authorization versus a third-party nondisclosure restriction.

guidance.procedure: Read the definition as a structured rule, not as a keyword match. For technical-only scope, determine whether every covered category is technical or whether commercial, financial, operational, oral, visual, documentary, or other material is also included. For identification requirements, distinguish an operative marking or designation condition from a mere description that information is confidential; also preserve exceptions for unmarked samples or inherently confidential material. For oral inclusion, collect both the form-inclusive definition and any designation, confirmation, or writing condition that controls coverage. For independent development and third-party acquisition, distinguish exclusions from confidentiality from permissions to obtain or develop similar information, and retain the no-access, lawful-source, nonconfidential, or no-restriction qualifications. Include definition lead-ins and continuation spans only when they jointly establish the rule; do not infer NotMentioned merely because a preferred phrase is absent.

operations.rationale: Creates a definition-boundary skill because historical answers confused broad definitions with technical-only coverage and sometimes treated descriptive confidentiality language as an identification mandate. The contrasting witnesses show technical-only and broader coverage, mandatory marking and coverage regardless of labeling, plus qualified independent-development and lawful-third-party exclusions.

complete_original_evidence_texts: WHEREAS, each party has certain technical information described below which shall hereinafter be referred to as "CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION";
a. As used herein, “Proprietary Information” means information that
(i) embodies trade secrets as defined under 18 U.S.C. § 1839 or

(ii) is commercial or financial information that is privileged or confidential under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(4)), and that is developed at private expense outside this Agreement.

a. Disclosing Party will identify and mark its written Proprietary Information or NREL Protected Information disclosed hereunder as “Proprietary Information” or “NREL Protected Information”, as applicable, at the time it is conveyed to Receiving Party.
For Proprietary Information or NREL Protected Information first disclosed orally (i.e., information expressed by spoken words) hereunder, Disclosing Party will:
(i) identify such information as Proprietary Information or NREL Protected Information, as applicable, at the time it is conveyed to Receiving Party;
(ii) reduce such information to writing; and
(iii) provide an appropriately identified and marked copy of such writing to Receiving Party within thirty (30) days of such disclosure.

For purposes of this Agreement, “Confidential Information” means all information and materials, in whatever form, whether tangible or intangible, disclosed by Companion Paws or The LifeLine Canada Foundation or any of its authorized representatives to Volunteer or Evaluator, or to which Volunteer, Trainer or Evaluator otherwise gains access as a result of volunteering or working for Companion Paws or The LifeLine Canada Foundation, pertaining in any manner to the activities of Companion Paws and The LifeLine Canada Foundation or its affiliates, consultants, members, or any person or entity to which Companion Paws ad The LifeLine Canada Foundation owes a duty of confidentiality, whether or not labeled or identified as proprietary or confidential.
1.1 "confidential information" –
is information which is confidential to FP and includes but is not limited to:

The following types of information, however marked, are not Confidential Information.
Information that:
